title: Egnyte Pricing 2026: Plans and Per-User Costs
summary: Egnyte pricing spans multiple tiers with different costs and features. Compare per-user rates, included capabilities, and usage restrictions per tier.
body_markdown:
## Controlling Egnyte Costs With Activepieces


Activepieces moves information between business apps across 750+ integrations, under an MIT-licensed core. It can't lower Egnyte's price, but it can stop you paying for seats nobody uses and warn you before storage runs out.


That's a narrow fit, and it helps to be plain about it. Whatever package you and the vendor agreed on stays the same. What changes is how well you keep to it.


Nobody notices, because nothing breaks: a person who left months ago still counts if no one removes them. Seat-based billing punishes neglect that way. **Doing nothing costs you every month, quietly** .


> Whatever package you and the vendor agreed on stays the same. What changes is how well you keep to it.


### Offboarding automation to free Egnyte seats


Start by tying Egnyte accounts to the system that already knows who works for you. That might be an HR platform or an identity provider (the service that handles staff logins).


When someone is marked as departed there, an Activepieces flow can fire and deactivate their Egnyte account, so the paid seat is released the same day instead of whenever someone remembers.


For new hires, the same flow can run in reverse, creating the account only when HR confirms a start.


### What a simple workflow looks like


To see the simplest version of a flow, a trigger followed by steps, look at the screenshot: one trigger step, labeled "1. new flavor created," attached to an "End" node.


Open the right-hand panel and it shows the trigger's setup, a connection to the app, and a "Generate Sample Data" section reporting "Loaded Successfully."


It's a demo using an ice-cream integration, not an Egnyte flow, but it shows what you would be maintaining: a trigger, a stored connection, and test data you can inspect before anything goes live.


### Check the Egnyte connector


Next, confirm the Egnyte connector has the specific actions you need, such as deactivating a user, before you plan around it.


Offboarding, provisioning and storage alerts don't have to share one fragile flow: Activepieces lists unlimited flows on every plan from Free through Ultimate and meters only credits per run, at one credit a run however many steps it has.


Zapier bills a task per action and Make a credit per module, so there the tidy split into three small flows costs more each time it runs.


If it doesn't, the fallback is a generic web request step against Egnyte's own interface, which takes more setup and someone who can maintain it.


### Storage and usage alerts


Second, a scheduled check can read your Egnyte usage and message you when it crosses a threshold you choose. Because storage is pooled, a warning early enough lets you clean up or renegotiate on your terms, not during a surprise overage.


Again, verify that the usage data you want is available through the integration or Egnyte's interface before you count on this.
